thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert triggered for service=inference-api, region=az1c. High 5xx rate + p95 token latency spike. Impact: ~12% of requests experiencing timeouts. PD: P1.

alex: seeing packet jitter across the az1c-subnet NAT path, a lot of SYN retransmits in the instance logs. tracing shows repeated connect timeouts to external resolve endpoints and kv cache misses.

sam: can you paste the native logs?

alex: pasting snippets
```
[2026-03-15T09:22:14Z] net: tcp retransmit seq=0/1400 rto=300ms, dst=10.0.45.12:443
[2026-03-15T09:22:18Z] tcp: connection reset by peer during TLS handshake
[2026-03-15T09:22:21Z] inference/predict: upstream request timeout after 2.5s (attempt 3)
```

riley: confirmed -- host-level metrics show RX/TX jitter on enic0 on a subset of g5 nodes. Egress NAT gateway pps spike correlates.

ops_oncall: paging the network on-call now. @infra-bot, start a cross-AZ traffic steer job in read-only mode.

infra-bot: acknowledged. queued traffic-steer-job id=ts-2365129876-1 (read-only dry-run).

alex: quick mitigation idea: steer a small percent of inference traffic off az1c to az1a/az1b using the routing policy ramp (10% -> 50% -> 100%), keep cache-priming nodes warm in target AZs to avoid cold-start regressions.

sam: agree. Start 10% immediately. Use low TTL DNS and edge routing weights. Also increase low-latency reserved capacity on az1a to absorb burst.

riley: running commands now:
```
# internal CLI - adjust routing weight to route 10% outbound from az1c -> az1a
rictl routing update --service inference-api --from az1c --to az1a --weight 10
# scale dedicated pool in az1a
rictl capacity adjust --pool inference-dedicated-az1a --add 8
```

infra-bot: routing change applied (id=ts-2365129876-1). Capacity adjust submitted to autoscaler (job=cap-8492).

alex: tests show request success rate improved for the 10% cohort, p95 tokens down from 1.8s -> 0.36s for redirected traffic. az1c still noisy though.

sam: initiate instance-level mitigations in az1c: drain most-affected nodes, restart nics, and disable NAT gateway path for those subnets so they egress via alternate ENI path.

riley: commands:
```
# identify top affected nodes
rictl nodes list --region az1c --sort net_errors | head -n 5
kubectl drain node/g5-az1c-045 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force
ssh ops@g5-az1c-045 "sudo ethtool -K enic0 rx off; sudo ethtool -K enic0 rx on; sudo systemctl restart network"
# reroute subnet egress to secondary route table
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-az1c-app --destination-cidr-block 0.0.0.0/0 --instance-id i-standby-nat-az1c
```

infra-bot: node drain requests accepted. NAT route replace queued (rtb-az1c-app -> i-standby-nat-az1c).

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created: PD-98321. Current status: mitigations in progress.

customer-success: can we get a short-canned message for affected customers? Some on-prem enterprise is watching.

sam: short msg: "We are investigating elevated inference errors from a single availability zone (az1c). Traffic is being rerouted to healthy capacity while we remediate the underlying network issue. You may see transient errors or increased latency for some requests. We will post updates every 15 minutes."

customer-success: posting to status.redwood.ai/incident/PD-98321 now.

alex: after draining 3 nodes and applying NIC restarts, node-level errors dropped 60% for those hosts, but overall az1c still shows elevated egress packet reordering on ~25% of hosts.

riley: suggestion: mark the az as degraded in the routing policy (fail fast) and expand reroute to 60% while we continue node remediation. That avoids overloading az1a all at once.

sam: agreed. ramp to 60% with a short cool-down (2 minutes) and monitor dropped requests.

riley: updated: rictl routing update --service inference-api --from az1c --to az1a --weight 60 --cooldown 120

infra-bot: routing update applied. Observability: error rate in the global service dropped from 12% -> 4% in 3 minutes. p95 token latency globally improved.

alex: note: some sessions are sticky; clients with cached DNS to az1c may still hit bad hosts. Lowered TTL to 30s earlier but might take a minute to propagate.

ops_oncall: one customer reported a higher error rate still. @sam can you open a dedicated support thread and offer a temporary key reroute to a specific regional endpoint?

sam: opened support/INC-7112, offered endpoint fallback and free retry-window config. Customer accepted fallback.

incident-bot: automatic postmortem checklist started. tagging: network, routing, nat-gateway, oncall-handoff.

riley: I'm taking the pager for the next 30m to see if the reroute fully stabilizes. handing off to me @sam.

sam: thanks — leaving notes: drained 5 nodes, replaced rtb route, increased az1a capacity by +8, routing ramped to 60%. If errors return, rollback is to 0% weight and failover to az2a as fallback.

riley: ack. I'll keep monitoring. current plan: continue node remediation, if pod eviction rate stays low and packet reorder drops below threshold then we will slowly return 20% of traffic after 45 minutes.

infra-bot: monitoring checks: enic_rx_err_rate, nat_gateway_pps, instance_net_jitter. Alert thresholds temporarily lowered for this incident.

alex: quick note for post-incident: evaluate NAT gateway autoscaling behaviour, route-table convergence times, and consider warm standby nodes across AZs to shorten failover. Also add a recipe to Redwood runbook for targeted subnet egress steering.

incident-bot: status update posted to status page. Next update ETA +15m.

customer-success: customers notified, support thread created for the one enterprise using pinned az endpoints. No data loss reported, only transient request errors/latency.

riley: final for now — error rate holding at ~3.5% (mostly retries resolved). continuing to monitor. taking the rest of the shift.

sam: thanks all. if anything spikes, re-pager. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident PD-98321 acknowledged by riley. will auto-close when metrics stable for 60 minutes and postmortem completed.
